newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX traders guardedly upbeat on Taiwan ban news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX traders guardedly upbeat on Taiwan ban news.

text.p: SIMEX traders welcomed news Taiwan's Finance Ministry had approved a proposal to legalise trading of offshore stock index futures on Wednesday but were guarded about how soon the ban might actually be lifted.
"It definitely will help. But the point here is how soon they're going to get it approved by the cabinet," a trader with a local institution said.
Taiwan Finance Minister Paul Chiu approved the proposal to lift the ban on Tuesday, a ministry official said, adding that it would be submitted to the cabinet for final approval as soon as possible.
"It'll be another week or two at least until they get it passed by the cabinet," a senior trader at another house said.

Under the liberalisation, Taiwan futures houses will be able to trade futures linked to the Taipei stock market's performance offered by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) and the Singapore International Monetary Exchange.

SIMEX and CME launched the contracts, based on the MSCI and Dow Jones Taiwan indices respectively, on January 9 against the objections of Taiwan regulators who wanted them to wait until Taipei could open its own futures market.
SIMEX officials were not immediately available for comment.

Liquidity in the SIMEX Taiwan stock index futures has picked up steadily since its launch and now averages over 2,000 lots daily. Traders said they expected the entry of Taiwanese customers to boost contract volumes further.
Meanwhile, trading of the SIMEX MSCI Taiwan stock index futures was relatively slow on Wednesday, the first day of May's status as the front month.
The May contract was at 349.0 at 0353 GMT against its opening 353.4 on volume of 775 lots.
The trader with the local institution said the contract looked a bit toppish on the short-term charts, but added that it could receive a boost from news of the proposal to lift the ban moving ahead.
"This should be positive for the market and in any case, the longer term trend is still up," he said.
